lines.japanese: 金を出してまでってほどじゃないんだけど、ちょろっと夕刊が読みたくて、俺は始発ホームで折り返し発進を待っている急行列車の網棚を、端から端まで探して歩いたんだ。
lines.english: I didn't want one badly enough to pay for it, but I kind of felt like skimming the evening paper. So I walked the length of an express waiting at the departure platform for its return run, checking every luggage rack from end to end.

lines.japanese: でもこんな日にかぎって、ぬるいエログラビアが売りのゴシップ週刊誌しか手に入らなかった。
lines.english: Of course, this was the one day all I could find was a gossip rag whose big selling point was some half-assed softcore pinups.

lines.japanese: 駅周辺のゴミ箱も最近はテロ対策だか何だかで、捨て口が小さくなっていたり、回収用の扉が施錠されていたり、透明の覗き窓が付いていたりする。
lines.english: Lately, because of terrorism or whatever, the trash cans around the station had tiny openings, locked collection doors, and clear windows you could look through.

lines.japanese: 世知辛い時代になったもんだよな。
lines.english: It’s a hard world we live in.

lines.japanese: ──と、透けて見える新聞紙を恨めしげに眺めつつぼやいたら、横にいた非認可のリサイクル業を営む住所不定のおっちゃんが、シミだらけの顔を得意げにほころばせた。
lines.english: —I muttered that while glaring bitterly at a newspaper visible through the clear panel. Beside me, a gentleman of no fixed address engaged in the unlicensed recycling trade broke into a proud smile across his mottled face.

lines.japanese: やつは先端が鉤状になってる鉄の棒を狭いゴミ捨て口に突っこむと、新聞の折り目に引っかけてそいつを器用にサルベージした。
lines.english: He stuck an iron rod with a hook on the end through the narrow opening, caught the newspaper by a fold, and fished it out like a pro.

lines.japanese: 芸能スポーツ中心のタブロイド紙じゃなくて、日本でいちばん読まれてるあの新聞だ。俺はおっちゃんの手際を誉めたたえてから、ゴシップ週刊誌と交換してもらった。
lines.english: And it wasn't some celebrity-and-sports tabloid. It was *that* paper, the most widely read in Japan. After praising the old man's technique to the skies, I got him to trade it for my gossip weekly.

lines.japanese: それからしばらくおっちゃんと話をした。もちろん初対面だけど、どうせ一期一会でお互い遠慮する必要がなかったせいか、わりと話は弾んだ。
lines.english: I talked with the old guy for a while after that. We'd just met, obviously, but maybe because we'd never see each other again and didn't need to hold back, we hit it off pretty well.

lines.japanese: おっちゃんは半生を捧げたカメラ屋が倒産する数十年前、大学で哲学を専攻していたそうで、ゴミ箱にまつわるよしなしごとをやたらと感慨深く語った。
lines.english: The old guy said he'd studied philosophy in college, decades before the camera shop he'd given half his life to went bust. He got really sentimental talking about all kinds of random trash-can stuff.

lines.japanese: たとえば雑誌ひとつ取っても、おっちゃんたちが拾いやすいようにわざわざゴミ箱の上へ平置きしていくやつもいれば、逆に拾われないよう表紙を破ってから投棄するやつもいるって話。
lines.english: Take a single magazine. Some people went out of their way to lay it flat atop the bin so men like him could collect it easily. Others tore off the cover before throwing it away expressly to keep anyone from collecting it.

lines.japanese: たとえばおっちゃんたちがゴミの持ち出ししていくのを、ある程度見て見ぬふりしてくれる業者もいれば、親の仇のごとく厳しく取りしまる役人もいるって話。
lines.english: Some businesses were willing, within reason, to pretend they hadn't seen his colleagues carry off the trash. Some officials cracked down as though the men had murdered their parents.

lines.japanese: 街には多様な恣意や故意が溢れ、それが一方では誰かを助け、また一方ではべつの誰かを困らせたりしている。なべて世は今日もそうして回るのだよ青年、とかって話。
lines.english: The city overflows with whims and intentions of every kind; here they help someone, there they trouble someone else. And thus, young man, the world continues to turn today. That sort of thing.

lines.japanese: 舌がノッたおっちゃんは、さらに言語の構造がもたらす人間性・社会性について一席ぶち始めたが、合間にエロ週刊誌をぱらぱらめくると、あるヌードモデルの奔放過ぎる陰毛について率直な不満を並べはじめた。
lines.english: Now thoroughly warmed to his theme, the old man launched into a lecture on human nature and social behavior produced by the structure of language. Then, leafing through the dirty weekly between observations, he began candidly listing his objections to one nude model’s excessively free-spirited pubic hair.

lines.japanese: 俺はそれを聞きながしながら、手に入れたばかりの夕刊をその場で広げた。三面記事と地方版にざっと目を通す。柳木原の小さな戦争は一行たりとも世間に知れわたっていなかった。
lines.english: I let him talk while I opened the evening paper I'd just gotten. I skimmed the crime and local pages. Not one line about Yanagihara's little war had made it out to the public.

lines.japanese: 俺はおっちゃんに新聞を返して駅をあとにした。キャッチ＆リリース。なべて世は今日もこうして回っておるのだよ。よく分かんねーけど。
lines.english: I gave the newspaper back to the old guy and left the station. Catch and release. Thus does the world keep turning today. Or something. Hell if I know.

lines.japanese: 今日は日曜日。パルさんの知り合いが飼ってる犬を一匹、２～３時間ばかり預かって面倒見る約束だ。
lines.english: Today was Sunday. I had promised to look after a dog belonging to an acquaintance of Paru's for two or three hours.

lines.japanese: ──ああ、訂正。犬と変な小娘を一匹ずつ、だった。
lines.english: —Ah, correction. One dog and one peculiar little girl.

lines.japanese: 俺は通りかかったケータイ販売店の店先から壁時計を覗いた。約束の時間にはまだちょっと早かった。
lines.english: As I passed a cell-phone shop, I peered in at the clock on the wall. I was still a little early for our appointment.

lines.japanese: マルチネスとアリスでもいじって暇を潰そうかと思ったけど、やつらはちょうどお巡りさんに怒られて露店を畳みはじめたところだった。
lines.english: I considered killing time by pestering Martinez and Alice, but they were just beginning to pack up their street stall under a policeman's scolding.

lines.japanese: ガード下の方から今日も聴こえてくるジェンベの音はちょっと気になったけれど、さすがにもう関わりたくないと思う気持ちの方が強かった。
lines.english: The djembe drifting from beneath the tracks again today did nag at my curiosity. Even so, my desire to have nothing more to do with that crowd was stronger.

lines.japanese: けっきょく俺は、いつものようにパイプベンチへ尻を載せてボケーッとした。ボケーッとして流れる人波を眺めるのは、それだけでわりと楽しい。
lines.english: In the end, I planted my ass on the usual pipe bench and went pleasantly blank. Letting my mind go empty while the human tide flowed past was fairly entertaining all by itself.

lines.japanese: 隣りのカップルの痴話喧嘩を盗み聞きするような遊び方もあるけど、そういう面白いおもちゃが転がってないときには耳を“開いて”みるといい。
lines.english: You could amuse yourself by eavesdropping on the lovers' quarrel beside you, but when no entertaining little toy happened to be lying around, you could try ‘opening’ your ears.

lines.japanese: なにか特定の音を聴きとろうとするんじゃなくて、街全体から湧きあがっている壮大な鳴き声みたいのを体に染みこませるイメージ。そうしていると自分が都会の一部に溶けこんで、いろんなものが見えてくるんだ。
lines.english: You don't try to pick out one sound. You picture the whole city making one huge animal cry and let it soak into your body. Do that and you start melting into the city yourself, and you can see all kinds of things.

lines.japanese: まあ、悟りっていうかただの錯覚なんだろうけどさ、でも突きつめていきゃ人間の感情なんてどれも脳味噌の錯覚みたいなもんだろ。こんなこと俺が言うのもなんだけど。
lines.english: Call it enlightenment—though it was probably just an illusion. But take the thought far enough and every human feeling is basically an illusion in the brain. Rich words, coming from me.

lines.japanese: そうして俺はコンクリートジャングルの森林浴で時間を潰してから、のんびり交差点を渡ってパルクレープへ向かった。
lines.english: After killing time with a little forest bathing in the concrete jungle, I strolled across the intersection toward Paru Crêpes.

lines.japanese: クレープ屋が見えてきたあたりで、正面から歩いてくる髪の長い女と目が合った。
lines.english: Just as the crêpe stand came into view, my eyes met those of a long-haired woman approaching from the other direction.

lines.japanese: どっかで見たような見ないような、一重まぶたの薄味な顔。すっぴんの眉は平安時代の殿上人みたいだ。女の少し先を、リードで繋がれた白黒ツートンカラーの小型犬がガニ股で歩いていた。
lines.english: A plain, single-lidded face I felt like I'd maybe seen somewhere, or maybe not. Without makeup, her eyebrows looked like a Heian court noble's. A little black-and-white dog waddled bowlegged ahead of her on a leash.

lines.japanese: 向こうもこちらを見て何か引っかかってる感じだったけれど、記憶を呼びおこすまでの決定打がなく、お互い声をかけたりはせずそのまま擦れちがった。
lines.english: She looked like something about me was nagging at her too, but neither of us had enough to jog the rest of the memory, so we passed without speaking.
Hm. Hmmm...?

lines.japanese: いまのはもしかして……前に一度会ったことがある……？
lines.english: Could that have been... someone I'd met once before...?

lines.japanese: 「パルさん」
lines.english: “Paru.”

lines.japanese: ミニバンへ辿りついた俺は、すぐに店主を呼んだ。
lines.english: The moment I reached the minivan, I called for its owner.

lines.japanese: 「ああドラ……早いね……」
lines.english: “Oh, Dra... You’re early...”

lines.japanese: 「あのさ、いま何とも幸薄そうな女と、ホルスタインをお茶の間サイズに絞ったような犬があっち歩いてったんだけど、アレひょっとして──」
lines.english: “Hey, I just passed a woman who looked pretty down on her luck, walking a dog like a Holstein scaled down for the living room. Was that maybe—”

lines.japanese: 「そうだドラ、今日はあたしがおごったげらあ。ねッ、もう、なんでも好きなもの頼みなさいよ」
lines.english: “That's right, Dra. Today's on me. Come on—order anything you like.”
“Huh?”

lines.japanese: 俺の話も聞かず、パルさんはとつぜん気前のいいことを言う。そんなときはいつもなにか裏がある。分かっててあっさり懐柔されるのも間抜けな話だ。
lines.english: Without listening to me, Paru had suddenly made a generous offer. There was always a catch when she did that. It would take a complete fool to know as much and still be bought so easily.

lines.japanese: 「いや、いいよ。だってほら、俺いまから仕事じゃん」
lines.english: “No, I'm good. I mean, I'm about to start work, aren't I?”

lines.japanese: 「あー、悪い……それな、ドタキャン喰らった」
lines.english: “Ah—sorry. About that. I got hit with a last-minute cancellation.”
“What?”

lines.japanese: 「いまアケミちゃんに会ったろ？　まあ実はな、管理人が予定より早い時間に来やがったもんで、犬飼ってることもうバレちまったんだってよ」
lines.english: “You just saw Akemi, right? Truth is, the building manager showed up earlier than planned, and she got caught with the dog.”

lines.japanese: 「ハァ？」
lines.english: “What?”

lines.japanese: 「だから隠す必要なくなったって。いまから不動産屋行ってペットＯＫな部屋探してくるってさ」
lines.english: “So there's no point hiding it now. She's heading to a real-estate agent to find a place that allows pets.”

lines.japanese: 「ハァァ？」
lines.english: “Whaaat?”

lines.japanese: 「というわけだから──ドラ、おごってやるよ。なんでも好きなの頼みな」
lines.english: “Which brings us back to this—Dra, my treat. Order anything you like.”

lines.japanese: そういうことか。俺は言葉を失った。
lines.english: So that was it. Words failed me.

lines.japanese: 「……ツナカレーチーズ」
lines.english: “...Tuna, curry, and cheese.”

lines.japanese: でも、もらえるものはもらっておくことにした。
lines.english: Still, I saw no reason not to take what was offered.

lines.japanese: 「悪いねえ。ツナ大盛りにしといてやるからさ、な、勘弁しとくれよ」
lines.english: “Sorry about this. I'll give you extra tuna, all right? So let me off the hook.”

lines.japanese: 「いや、まあ……べつにパルさん悪くねーし仕方ねえよ」
lines.english: “Yeah, well... It isn't your fault, Paru. Nothing you could do.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、ああ……そうかい……？」
lines.english: “Ah. Right... is that so...?”

lines.japanese: 俺が後ろ頭をがしがし掻きながら言うと、パルさんはちょっと驚いたみたいに硬く微笑んだ。
lines.english: I said it while raking hard at the back of my head. Paru gave me a stiff little smile, as though I'd surprised her.

lines.japanese: それにしても、最近はどうもこんなのばっかだ。エージからの仕事は論外にしても、パルさんからの仕事でも上手いこと折り合いがつかない。
lines.english: Still, this seemed to be all I got lately. Eiji’s jobs were out of the question, and even the work from Paru never came together properly.

lines.japanese: 「まあ、もともと無理はあったんだよな、ガキのままごとみてーな手伝いして金の足しにする商売なんてさ」
lines.english: “I guess the whole business was always asking too much. Scraping together spending money from chores that amount to kids playing house...”

lines.japanese: 俺は日曜日の歓楽街を眺めながらしみじみ呟いた。
lines.english: I gazed across the Sunday entertainment district and murmured the thought aloud.

lines.japanese: 「ぼちぼち潮時……かねぇ……」
lines.english: “Maybe it's about time... I packed it in.”

lines.japanese: バーガー屋のねーちゃんが、店先でたむろしてる中学生たちに頭を下げながらホーキをかけていた。俺より年下みたいだけど、休みの日に御苦労さんだ。
lines.english: A girl from the burger place was sweeping out front, bowing apologetically to the middle-schoolers loitering in her way. She looked younger than me, yet there she was working hard on a Sunday.

lines.japanese: ミニバンに向きなおると、クレープ屋が目を丸くしてじっと俺を見つめていた。
lines.english: When I turned back to the minivan, the crêpe seller was staring at me, eyes wide.

lines.japanese: 「なに」
lines.english: “What?”

lines.japanese: 「いや……なんだ……ま、なんてこたァないんだけど……ドラ、最近ちょっと変わったかも？」
lines.english: “No... It's nothing. Nothing much, anyway... Dra, have you changed a little lately?”

lines.japanese: 「ハァ？　そうかあ？」
lines.english: “Huh? Have I?”

lines.japanese: 俺は顔をしかめて体ごと引いた。変わっただなんて、ふん、どこかのニワトリみたいなことを口にする。
lines.english: I scowled and drew my whole body back. *Changed,* she said. Hmph. She sounded like a certain Chicken.

lines.japanese: ニワトリ……。
lines.english: Chicken...

lines.japanese: ふと、ゆうべの現実離れした騒動を思いだす。鳳翔。やつは左肩に受けた傷をどうしただろう。やはり病院には行ってないのだろうか。
lines.english: All of a sudden I remembered last night's unreal mess. Kakeru Otori. What had he done about the wound in his left shoulder? Had he really not gone to a hospital?

lines.japanese: これは前にやつから聞いた話。柳木原駅からタクシーを十五分ぐらい走らせた住宅街の中に、外からはごく普通の一戸建てにしか見えない、庭のツツジが見事に刈りそろえられた二階建ての家があるらしい。
lines.english: He had once told me this story. Fifteen minutes by taxi from Yanagihara Station, in a residential neighborhood, there was supposedly a two-story house that looked perfectly ordinary from the outside, with azaleas in the garden clipped to immaculate precision.

lines.japanese: チャイムを押してインターホンに秘密の合言葉を唱えると、暴力団の幹部みたいな目付きをした初老のおっさんが現れて、汚いダイニングへ案内される。そこには黄ばんだシーツの敷かれた、簡素な寝台がある。
lines.english: Ring the bell and recite a secret password into the intercom, and an older man with the eyes of a mob boss would appear and lead you into a filthy dining room. There stood a plain cot covered by yellowed sheets.

lines.japanese: キッチンの戸棚には、インスタントコーヒーやグラニュー糖と一緒に、メスや鉗子や注射器が並んでいる。
lines.english: The kitchen cupboards held scalpels, forceps, and syringes alongside instant coffee and granulated sugar.

lines.japanese: 深刻な処置を受けている最中、隣りの居間から聞こえてくるのは、深夜なら海外の通販番組の吹き替えボイス、明け方ならニュースを読む女子アナの声。
lines.english: While some grave procedure was underway, the soundtrack from the next room would be dubbed voices from an overseas infomercial late at night, or a female announcer reading the news toward dawn.

lines.japanese: 闇医者──なんて存在は極道ものの劇画やＶシネマが広めた都市伝説だと思ってたけど、鳳に言わせれば「いるところにはいる」ものらしい。
lines.english: A black-market doctor—I had assumed creatures like that were an urban legend spread by gangster comics and straight-to-video crime films. Otori claimed that if you knew where to look, they were out there.

lines.japanese: どこまで本当なんだか。俺は話半分で聞いたもんだ。
lines.english: Who knew how much of it was true. I took the story with a grain of salt.

lines.japanese: 「あいよっ、ツナカレーチーズお待ち！」
lines.english: “Here you go! Tuna, curry, and cheese!”

lines.japanese: 「あ……ああ、さんきゅ」
lines.english: “Ah... right. Thanks.”

lines.japanese: ピンク色の円錐にくるまれたクレープを受けとる。包装紙越しに温度が伝わった。いつもながら美味そうだ。カレーの匂いも食欲をそそる。
lines.english: I accepted the crêpe in its cone of pink paper. Warmth came through the wrapper. It looked as good as ever, and the smell of curry sharpened my appetite.

lines.japanese: 慌ててがっついたら火傷しそうなぐらいほかほかだけど、１１月の終わりには丁度いいと思う。俺は冷めるまで待ちきれなくて、勢いよくふーふーしながら食った。
lines.english: It was hot enough to burn me if I wolfed it down, but just right for late November. I couldn't wait for it to cool, so I ate while blowing hard on every bite.

lines.japanese: 「パルさんさぁ」
lines.english: “Hey, Paru.”

lines.japanese: ふー、ふー。
lines.english: I blew on it. Then blew again.
“Mm?”

lines.japanese: 「こういうとこで店出してっと、やっぱ、ヤバい筋のおっさんとか来んの」
lines.english: “When you run a stand in a place like this, do seriously shady guys ever come around?”

lines.japanese: 「はあ？　なんだい、藪から棒に」
lines.english: “Huh? Where'd that come from?”

lines.japanese: 「いや、べつに、なんとなくだけど」
lines.english: “Nowhere. Just wondering.”

lines.japanese: 「ああ……まあ、それなりにな」
lines.english: “Yeah... some.”

lines.japanese: 「それなりにイチャモン付けられんの」
lines.english: “And they give you some shit?”

lines.japanese: 「いや、て言うか……まあ、それなりに渡してっから」
lines.english: “No, I mean... I hand over a little something.”

lines.japanese: 「渡してるって……え、みかじめ料ってやつ？」
lines.english: “Hand over—what, protection money?”

lines.japanese: 「おい、ちょっと、滅多なこと言わないどくれ。そういうのは渡した方も警察に目ぇ付けられンだ」
lines.english: “Hey, watch what you say. The police keep an eye on the people who pay that sort of thing too.”

lines.japanese: 「でも払ってんだ」
lines.english: “But you do pay it.”

lines.japanese: 「違うんだよ。ちょいと高めの、おしぼりとか植木とか張り子の虎を買ってんだよ」
lines.english: “It’s different. I buy slightly overpriced wet towels, potted plants, papier-mâché tigers...”

lines.japanese: 「あ？　なにそれ、この店そんなん使わねーじゃん」
lines.english: “Huh? What for? You don't use any of that here.”

lines.japanese: 「役所みたいなこと言うんじゃないよ。いいだろ、デリケートな問題なんだから」
lines.english: “Don't talk like City Hall. Drop it. It's a delicate subject.”

lines.japanese: 「でも、むりやり買わされてんだろ。押し売りじゃん。プチ脅迫じゃん。お巡りさんに言っちゃえよ」
lines.english: “But they're forcing you to buy it, right? That's a shakedown. Extortion Lite. Tell a cop.”

lines.japanese: 「警察？　ハッ、そりゃ無理な話だ。うちだってコレ、道交法ぶっちぎって商売してんだから」
lines.english: “The police? Hah. Fat chance. This operation of mine already drives a truck straight through the traffic laws.”

lines.japanese: 「ああ、それもそっか」
lines.english: “Oh. Right. There's that too.”

lines.japanese: 「それにな、まあ、何も嫌々払ってるわけじゃないんだよ。酔っ払いとかホームレスとか中国系の筋モンとか、他のタチ悪い客に絡まれたときなんか、ちゃんと助けてくれるしさ」
lines.english: “Besides, it's not like I pay them for nothing. If a drunk, a homeless guy, some Chinese outfit, or any other nasty customer gives me trouble, they really do step in.”

lines.japanese: 「他にも、そうさなあ……同業同士の場所取りとかで揉めないよう面倒見てくれたりさ。あと噂じゃ、裏で手ぇ回して警察の取り締まりを牽制してくれてるとかって話も聞くし」
lines.english: “They do other things too. They keep vendors from fighting over spots, for one. And rumor has it they pull strings behind the scenes to discourage police crackdowns.”

lines.japanese: 「へえー」
lines.english: “Huh.”

lines.japanese: なんつうか、微妙な話だ。一面的にはまともな商談っぽくも聞こえるけど、でも見えないどこかでその金は、悪どい組織の活動資金になってるんじゃないのか。
lines.english: I dunno. It was kind of a weird deal. From one side, it sounded like a normal business transaction, but somewhere out of sight, wasn't that money funding some nasty organization?

lines.japanese: なべて世は、だ。
lines.english: Such was the way of the world.

lines.japanese: 「まあ、オフィス街とか郊外のスーパーでちゃんとショバ借りてね、警察と保健所からも正規の許可もらって、堂々と商売する手もあるっちゃあるんだけど」
lines.english: “I suppose I *could* rent a proper space in an office district or outside some suburban supermarket, get legitimate permits from the police and health department, and do business openly.”

lines.japanese: 「だけど？」
lines.english: “But?”

lines.japanese: 「あいにくあたしゃ、このごちゃごちゃしためんどくさい街が気に入っててねえ」
lines.english: “Trouble is, I'm fond of this cluttered, pain-in-the-ass town.”

lines.japanese: 「あー」
lines.english: “Ah.”

lines.japanese: ネオ屋台の若き女店主は、親指で鼻の頭を弾いてふんと笑った。
lines.english: The young woman behind the mobile food stand flicked the tip of her nose with her thumb and gave a defiant snort.

lines.japanese: 「何度か臨海の方で店広げたりもしたんだけどな、どうもあの辺は駄目だね、あたしの性にゃ合わないよ。街も道も無駄に広すぎらあ。しゃらくせえ、綺麗で新しいけど、そんだけだい」
lines.english: “I tried setting up by the waterfront a few times, but that place is no good. Doesn't suit me. The town and the roads are both pointlessly huge. Too damned pleased with itself. Clean and new, sure, but that's all.”

lines.japanese: 「そりゃたしかに人ァ多かったよ？　あァ、客も多かった。だけど、なんーだかスカしたガキばっかでねえ。その点、柳木原は老若男女変なやつがいっぱいいて面白えや。ええドラ、あんただってそう思うだろ」
lines.english: “Oh, there were plenty of people. Plenty of customers too. But every last one was some affected little brat. Yanagihara's full of weirdos, young and old, men and women. Much more interesting. Come on, Dra—you think so too.”

lines.japanese: 「んー、まあ……そうだな」
lines.english: “Mm. Yeah... I guess I do.”

lines.japanese: 俺もアニキの真似をして鼻を弾いた。それからツナカレーチーズを食いおえて、あとに残った包装紙をゴミ箱に投げいれた。
lines.english: I copied the boss and flicked my own nose. Then I finished the tuna-curry-cheese crêpe and tossed the empty wrapper into the trash.

lines.japanese: 「ごっそさん」
lines.english: “Thanks. That hit the spot.”

lines.japanese: それから俺は、乱立する下品な風俗ビルを眺めてしばらく立ちつくした。
lines.english: Then I stood for a while, gazing at the sleazy adult-entertainment buildings jostling for space on every side.

lines.japanese: 「いや、でも参ったな。これからどうすっか……」
lines.english: “Still, this puts me in a bind. What the hell do I do now...?”

lines.japanese: 食いおわったのはいいけど、さて、このままひとりで帰路へつくわけにもいかない。俺はまた例によって後ろ頭をがしがし掻いていた。
lines.english: Fine, I'd finished eating, but I couldn't exactly head home alone now. Once again, I scratched hard at the back of my head.

lines.japanese: 「ん？　なにがよ？」
lines.english: “Mm? What’s the matter?”

lines.japanese: 「いや、パルさん責める気はないけどさ。仕事ポシャるんだったら、あいつ呼ぶんじゃなかった」
lines.english: “I'm not blaming you, Paru. But if I'd known the job would fall through, I wouldn't have called her.”

lines.japanese: 「あいつって？」
lines.english: “Called who?”

lines.japanese: 「あ、いや、なんか暇そうだったから誘ったんだよ。ほら、あいつ──」
lines.english: “Ah, well, she looked like she had time to kill, so I invited her. You know, she—”

lines.japanese: 「だーれだー」
lines.english: “Guess whooo?”

lines.japanese: 「いででででっ……ちょっ馬鹿、めーめーめー、目に爪っ……」
lines.english: “Ow ow ow ow... You idiot, wait, my-my-my eye! Your nails are in my—”

lines.japanese: 俺は謎の（いや、ぜんぜん謎じゃねーけど）目つぶし攻撃を引きはがして振りむいた。
lines.english: I peeled the mystery—okay, not remotely mysterious—eye-gouging attack off my face and turned around.

lines.japanese: 「えー、正解はー、恋の予感はブラインドネス鳳鳴さんでしたー」
lines.english: “And the answer iiis... Naru Otori—because love is blind!”

lines.japanese: いつもの制服とは違った装いの小娘が、てのひらをこっちに向けてにたにた笑っていた。
lines.english: The little girl, dressed in something other than her usual uniform, held one palm toward me and grinned.

lines.japanese: 「いってえ……てめ、なんだよ。なんだよいきなり」
lines.english: “Ow... What the hell? What was that out of nowhere?”

lines.japanese: 「こんばんはー。今日はデートっぽい登場を果たしてみましたよー」
lines.english: “Good evening. I thought I'd make a properly date-like entraaance.”

lines.japanese: 「いや、慣れねーことすんなって。おま、爪立ってたっつうの。おー痛て……」
lines.english: “Don't try stunts you aren't used to. You had your nails out. God, that hurts...”

lines.japanese: 「綺麗な薔薇には棘がありますよー」
lines.english: “Every beautiful rose has thorns.”

lines.japanese: 「あァ、なんだ。あんたら、一緒に散歩するつもりだったんだ？」
lines.english: “Ohh, I see. You two were planning to go for a walk together?”

lines.japanese: 「はいー、ドラさんからの強い要望ですー」
lines.english: “Yes. At Dra's passionate insistence.”

lines.japanese: 「ほぉー」
lines.english: “Oh-ho.”

lines.japanese: パルさんがこっちを向く。俺は無言のまま首を横に十回ぐらい振った。
lines.english: Paru turned to me. Without a word, I shook my head about ten times.

lines.japanese: 「それであのー、ふたりを取りもつ噂のキューピッド犬はどこにいるんですかー」
lines.english: “Sooo, where is the famous Cupid Dog who's going to bring the two of us together?”

lines.japanese: 鳴は片目をつぶって、見えない弓を引きしぼるジェスチャーを始めた。
lines.english: Naru closed one eye and began miming the draw of an invisible bow.

lines.japanese: 「あー、それなんだけどな。悪りぃ、もう犬の面倒見る必要なくなったんだわ」
lines.english: “Ah. About that. Sorry, but I don't need to look after the dog anymore.”

lines.japanese: 「はい？　そうなんですか？」
lines.english: “What? You don’t?”

lines.japanese: 「はい。そうなんです」
lines.english: “Yes. That's right.”

lines.japanese: やつが見えない弓弦から指を離した。俺は見えない恋の矢を片手で掴み、両手で折って捨てた。
lines.english: She loosed her invisible bowstring. I caught the invisible arrow of love in one hand, snapped it in two with both hands, and threw it away.

lines.japanese: 「いやー、ごめんな鳴、あたしからも謝るわ」
lines.english: “Ah, sorry, Naru. I should apologize too.”

lines.japanese: 「え？　あーいえいえ、構いませんよー。それじゃあ今日は人間だけで参りましょうかー」
lines.english: “Oh? No, no, it's quite all right. In that case, shall we proceed today with humans alone?”
“Huh?”

lines.japanese: 鳴は口元を隠してうぷぷと笑っていた。
lines.english: Naru hid her mouth and snickered.

lines.japanese: 「え、行くって、どこ行くの」
lines.english: “Wait, where are we going?”

lines.japanese: 「そうですねー、デートの行き先は男のひとが決めますよー」
lines.english: “Let's see. On a date, the gentleman chooses the destination.”

lines.japanese: 俺は眉をしかめたままクレープ屋に伺いを立てた。
lines.english: Still frowning, I asked the crêpe vendor what was up.

lines.japanese: 「え、なに、どーゆーこと」
lines.english: “Wait, what? What does that mean?”

lines.japanese: 「あたしに聞くなよ。だから『犬の』じゃなくて『散歩』の方が主目的だったんだろ」
lines.english: “Don't ask me. The main point was the ‘walk,’ wasn't it? Not the ‘dog.’”

lines.japanese: 「ハァ？　なんでよ」
lines.english: “Huh? Why?”

lines.japanese: 「あたしに聞くなってんだよ。いいから、とにかく行ってきなさいよ。今日はあんたから誘ったんだろ」
lines.english: “I told you, don't ask me. Just go. You're the one who invited her today.”

lines.japanese: 「誘ってねーよ。あ、いや、誘ったか。あれ、ほんとだ、誘ったかも」
lines.english: “I did not. Ah—no, I guess I did. Huh. I really might have.”

lines.japanese: 「あのー」
カウンター越しにパルさんと話してたら、遠慮がちな声が挿しこまれた。振りむいてみると、鳴は見上げ方まで遠慮がちになっていた。
lines.english: We were talking over the counter when a hesitant voice slipped between us. I turned. Even the way Naru looked up at me had grown hesitant.

lines.japanese: 「えとー、ひょっとして、いま私やっちゃってます？」
lines.english: “Um... am I making this weird?”

lines.japanese: 「あ？　なにを」
lines.english: “Huh? What did you do?”

lines.japanese: 「や、あの、もしあれでしたら今日はお開きということに。ええ、もう、実は私も所用がありました。はい、ありました。はい、たちどころに解散いたしましょう」
lines.english: “No, um, if this is inconvenient, we can call it a day. Yes, I actually had an errand too. I did. Yes. Let us disband immediately.”

lines.japanese: 鳴はいつもみたいに笑ってる。でも、なんか違う……あの変に間延びした喋り方じゃない。なんだかテンパってる小鳩みたいだ。
lines.english: Naru was smiling like always. But something was off... she wasn't doing that weird stretched-out way of talking. She sounded like Kobato when she was panicking.

lines.japanese: パルさんが険しい目で俺を睨み、顎先を小さく前へ突きだした。ふん、言われなくても。俺は親指で鼻を弾いてみせた。
lines.english: Paru glared daggers at me and gave a tiny thrust of her chin. Hmph. She didn't need to tell me. I flicked the tip of my nose with my thumb.

lines.japanese: 「馬鹿、冗談だっつの」
lines.english: “Idiot. I was joking.”

lines.japanese: それから鳴の額にちょっとだけ強めのデコピンを入れた。やつは驚いたのか、あうっと呻いて、大きく仰けぞった。
lines.english: Then I gave Naru a slightly harder flick on the forehead than necessary. Maybe it startled her; she yelped and reeled dramatically backward.

lines.japanese: 「んな、いちいち気にしてんじゃねーよ。そんなんじゃ今後、迂闊にパーティージョークも言えなくなるじゃねーか」
lines.english: “Quit worrying about every little thing. At this rate I won't be able to risk making a dumb joke around you.”

lines.japanese: 「はー」
lines.english: “Oh.”

lines.japanese: 鳴は両手でデコを押さえながら、ぽっかり口を開けて俺を見上げた。
lines.english: Holding her forehead in both hands, Naru stared up at me with her mouth hanging open.

lines.japanese: 「どうせ俺も暇なんだよ。おー、ほら、じゃあどっか適当にぶらつこうぜ」
lines.english: “I've got nothing to do either. Come on, let's wander around somewhere.”

lines.japanese: 「えー、ほんとですかー、無理してないですかー」
lines.english: “Really? You aren't forcing yourself?”

lines.japanese: やつはまだデコをさすっていた。言っちゃ悪いが似合ってる。思わず笑いがこみあげてきた。
lines.english: She was still rubbing her forehead. It suited her, though I hated to say so. A laugh rose in me before I could stop it.

lines.japanese: 「してねえよ。なんで俺がおまえに気ィ使わなきゃいけねーんだよ」
lines.english: “I'm not. Why the hell would I go out of my way to spare *your* feelings?”

lines.japanese: 「あー、そうですよねー。使いませんよねー」
lines.english: “Ah, of course. You wouldn't, would you?”

lines.japanese: 「やー、少しは使いましょうよー」
lines.english: “Come on, show a little consideration.”

lines.japanese: 俺は聞こえないふりをしてピンクのミニバンを振りかえった。
lines.english: I pretended not to hear and looked back at the pink minivan.

lines.japanese: 「パルさん、ゴチっす。ほんじゃ俺ら、ちょっと行ってくっから」
lines.english: “Paru, thanks for the grub. A'right, we're gonna head out for a bit.”

lines.japanese: 「……なあドラ」
lines.english: “...Say, Dra.”

lines.japanese: クレープ屋はにやにや笑って、すでに一度言ったことをまたぞろ飽きもせずに繰りかえした。
lines.english: The crêpe seller grinned and, apparently not yet tired of the subject, repeated what she had already said once.

lines.japanese: 「やっぱりおまえさん、なんか変わったんじゃないかい？　あたしゃいままで、あんたの口から『俺ら』なんて言葉が出るの、ついぞ聞いたことなかったけどねえ？」
lines.english: “You really have changed, haven'tcha? Never once heard ‘we’ come outta your mouth before, and I've known you a long time.”

lines.japanese: だから俺も、さっきと同じ言葉を返してやった。
lines.english: So I gave her the same answer as before.

lines.japanese: 「そうかあ？」
lines.english: “Have I?”

lines.japanese: 「さー、れっつごーですよー」
lines.english: “Come on. Let's gooo.”

lines.japanese: 俺がクレープ屋に背を向けると、鳴は浮わついた足取りで先に立って進みだした──
lines.english: I turned my back on the crêpe seller, and Naru set off ahead of me with a buoyant step—

lines.japanese: ──のはいいけど、どこへ行くつもりなんだ、あいつ。いくら目的地が決まってないっても、そんな、のぞき部屋とか裏ＤＶＤ屋の並ぶ路地へ入っていく必要はない。俺はあとを追いながら呼びとめた。
lines.english: —fine, but where the hell was she going? We didn't have a destination, sure, but that didn't mean she had to walk into an alley full of peep rooms and bootleg-DVD shops. I hurried after her and called out.

lines.japanese: 「おう、ちょーちょー。ちょっと待て小娘」
lines.english: “Hey, whoa, whoa. Hold up, little girl.”

lines.japanese: 「はいー？　なんですかー、告白ですかー」
lines.english: “Yes? Are you about to confess your love?”

lines.japanese: 「うるせえよ。いいから向こう行くぞオラ」
lines.english: “Shut up. We're going this way. Come on.”

lines.japanese: 俺は振りかえった鳴の腕を掴んで、人通りの多い方へ誘導した。
lines.english: I caught her arm when she turned and steered her toward the busier street.

lines.japanese: 「ええー、うはー、今日の彼ってばちょっぴり強引ー」
lines.english: “Ooh! My date's being a little forceful today.”

lines.japanese: 「テンション高けぇなあ」
lines.english: “You are *way* too excited.”
